title: Nifty posts best single-day gain since April, crosses 24,500 for first time in three months - The HinduBusinessLine
text:
Markets closed sharply higher on Thursday, logging their sixth consecutive session of gains, as a near 9 per cent crash in Brent crude and the Democratic sweep of the US midterm elections rewired global sentiment in India’s favour almost overnight.

The Nifty 50 closed at 24,536.60, up 576 points or 2.40 per cent, its sharpest single-day percentage gain since April 8, 2026, and its highest close in nearly three months. The Sensex settled at 79,310.01, up 2,008.61 points or 2.60 per cent. Bank Nifty outperformed both, surging 1,860.05 points or 3.33 per cent to close at 57,773.65. The Nifty has now gained over 8 per cent across the six-session streak, its strongest such run since February 2021.

“This was the sixth straight day of gains and the first clean break above the 24,000 level on the Nifty, which had capped the index through the recovery,” said Hemant Sood, Founder and Managing Director of Findoc Group, adding that investors added roughly ₹7 trillion in market value in a single session.

The rally was broad-based. Of 38 BSE sectoral indices, 36 advanced. Auto led with gains of over 4 per cent, followed by financial services, realty and private banks. The IT index, which had lagged for two sessions, rebounded more than 2 per cent. Media and Defence were the only notable laggards. Nifty Midcap 100 rose 1.90 per cent and Nifty Smallcap 100 gained 0.56 per cent, with the BSE advance-decline ratio at 2.06.

Bajaj Finance and Shriram Finance led Nifty 50 gainers, while Apollo Hospitals, ONGC and NTPC were the key laggards, a pattern Sood described as an “oil-and-rates rally,” where energy and public sector utilities lagged in line with falling crude.

Brent crude was trading near $94–96 per barrel, well below last week’s levels, after the Democratic midterm victory raised expectations of a US-Iran diplomatic resolution. WTI hovered around $86–87. Vinit Bolinjkar, Head of Research at Ventura, noted the clearest beneficiaries were “fuel- and crude-linked cost structures at IndiGo, Asian Paints and CEAT,” while “sustained lower oil prices could weaken realisations for ONGC and Oil India.” NSE cash-market turnover jumped 30 per cent from the previous session.

The rupee strengthened for a fifth straight session, appreciating 17 paise to 94.47 per dollar, its highest level since June 30, 2026, supported by softer crude, a weaker dollar index near 101.5 and continued foreign inflows. FIIs have now bought approximately ₹17,236 crore in the first three sessions of November alone. Gold on COMEX traded near $4,100–4,147, with MCX Gold around ₹1,45,680, rising on a weaker dollar rather than safe-haven demand.

Looking ahead, Ajit Mishra, SVP–Research at Religare Broking, said the Nifty is “on course to retest its August high of around 24,800,” with banking and financial stocks providing additional support. The key variables remain whether a formal US-Iran agreement materialises, whether Brent holds below $95, and the RBI’s December policy stance. Sood cautioned that “India VIX rose nearly 3 per cent even as the market climbed, which suggests participants are hedging rather than chasing”, a signal that after a six-session, 1,900-point rally, some consolidation cannot be ruled out.
